walkthroughs.body_html: The ONS 2021 Census recorded 59.6 million in England and Wales. Those identifying as White fell to 81.7% (from 86% in 2011), while Asian, Asian British rose to 9.3% and Black, Black British to 4.0%. London is now 36.8% White British. For the first time, fewer than half of Londoners (46.2%) identified as White overall. Christianity dropped below 50% (46.2%) while those reporting no religion rose to 37.2%.

Sociologist Steven Vertovec coined super-diversity to describe how UK cities are no longer characterised by one or two minority groups but by layered diversity across nationality, legal status, language, faith and migration channel. Newham contains over 100 languages spoken; Leicester is the first major UK city without a White ethnic majority. This complicates traditional ethnic monitoring categories.

Diversity is geographically uneven. London, Birmingham, Manchester, Bradford, Leicester and Luton show high diversity, while rural Wales, Cornwall and north-east England remain over 95% White British. This produces tensions in place identity: cosmopolitan global cities versus monocultural heritage towns, evident in the 2016 Brexit vote geography where diverse cities voted Remain and less diverse towns voted Leave.

mcqs.q: What happens in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?
options: The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.
Birth rates rise rapidly because people want larger families.
Death rates fall rapidly (due to better food, sanitation and medicine) while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.

mcqs.q: Why is the Demographic Transition Model criticised for not applying to all countries?
options: The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.

It was based on European industrialisation. LICs today face different conditions: imported medicine without industrialisation, cultural factors, gender inequality and globalised economies — not all follow the same path.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
All countries follow the five stages of the DTM in order.

mcqs.q: What is the 'race to the bottom' critique of globalisation?
options: The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.
The race to the bottom means TNCs compete with each other for the lowest prices.

The argument that TNCs play countries off against each other, relocating to those with lowest wages, weakest regulation and lowest taxes — pressuring governments to cut standards to attract investment.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
